title: Cascading Failure in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores cascading failure dynamics within a ring communication topology. A single node/link failure disrupts the sequential information flow, causing delayed decision-making and leading to physical route congestion and capacity exhaustion.

cascading-failure.details: Agent 'b' loses ability to pass messages to 'c', forcing information to travel the long way (b->a->d->c), creating 3x latency in coordination.

edge_cases_to_watch: Information stale-ness: Agents acting on outdated route availability data due to ring latency
Deadlock: Two agents waiting for a bridge that is blocked by a third agent rerouted due to the initial failure
Echo Chamber effect: Localized rerouting creates a feedback loop of congestion in the remaining functional segment
coordination_challenges: Increased message latency: Ring diameter increases effectively when a node/link fails
Split-brain coordination: Agents on one side of the break may optimize for local flow, inadvertently causing bottlenecks for agents on the other side
Priority conflict: High-priority jobs require immediate bandwidth, but ring latency prevents preemptive negotiation
suggested_agent_strategies: Predictive Buffering: Agents anticipate congestion on adjacent routes based on historical latency patterns
Redundant Signaling: Agents attempt to broadcast critical updates through multiple paths if the ring allows
Consensus-Light Protocol: Switching from global optimization to local-neighborhood optimization to reduce communication overhead during high-latency periods
Priority-Based Throttling: Deliberately delaying 'normal' priority jobs to reserve capacity for high-priority 'med-kit' or 'food' jobs

coordination_challenges: Increased message latency via ring topology

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimization of total system delay compared to no-failure baseline
